newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: HEAVY IMPORT PRESSURE DRIVES ZIMBABWE DLR WEAKER.
newsitem.headline: HEAVY IMPORT PRESSURE DRIVES ZIMBABWE DLR WEAKER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar lost over three cents against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, as it continued to be driven down on major currencies by heavy local import pressure, foreign exchange dealers said.
"After some breather in mid-morning, the market got hectic and volatile again. There was more pressure and it (the Zimbabwe dollar) lost ground against the U.S. dollar," one dealer said.
"There are no meaningful (foreign exchange) receipts flowing in...and the pressure is building all round and affecting the rating on the other currencies," he said.
The Zimbabwe dollar -- which was quoted at 10.4345/4500 at 0830 GMT against the U.S. dollar -- closed the day at 10.4550/4750 versus its Wednesday closing rate of 10.4125/4325.
It had fallen to 16.3610/4000 on pound sterling from 16.2960/3320, and also to 6.8360/8510 against the German mark compared to 6.8040/8190.
The local unit ended Thursday little changed against the South African rand at 2.2930/3010 versus 2.2940/3000.
